group.passage:
Superstitions abound, wherever you are in the world. Whether you take them with a pinch of salt, snort at them, or are a firm believer, a look at some of them provides a guide to do’s and don’ts if we ever find ourselves in strange lands.
Placing two mirrors opposite each other, and you create infinite reflections. However in Mexico, it is believed to open a doorway for the devil, and an infinite amount of bad luck. (1)______.
In the Philippines, people avoid going straight back home after a wake or a funeral, lest a bad spirit would tag along. Mourners usually make a stop at a restaurant or a park first, just in case some things follow them uninvited.
In Asia, gifting anything with a blade is commonly thought to sever a relationship. So if you can’t say no to the samurai sword your uncle gives you, give him a coin in return. (2)______.
You’re dining with some Europeans when someone proposes a toast. You find your wine glass empty and water glass full. (3)______ Greek mythology has many Europeans believe that offering a toast with water is no different from wishing death upon the people you’re drinking with.
Don’t sleep with your head to the north if you’re are in Japan, nor should you sleep with your head to the west in Africa. In each place, that’s how the deceased are laid to rest.
If you are in Britain and want to show off your new shoes to your friends, put them on the floor, never on the table. In the old days, this was a way to let people know someone in the family had passed way. (4)______.
If you find yourself laughing at the above superstitions, perhaps what happened to Arnold Schönberg, the Austrian composer, would sway you. A person with great Triskaidekaphobia, the fear of the number 13, Schöenberg was reminded that his age added up to 13 when he turned 76 in 1951. He was convinced that he would not survive to 77. He died later that year on Friday, July 13th.

figures.label: 第4題選項圖片 (A)–(D)
figures.caption: 第4題：四個選項皆為卡通插圖（原卷為灰階印刷）
figures.description: (A) 一雙懶人帆布便鞋（鞋面有波浪花紋、厚鞋底），放在木條拼成的地板上；(B) 一名綁著馬尾、面帶微笑的女生，穿著圓點洋裝、肚子明顯隆起（看似懷孕），右手拿著一把剪刀舉在胸前，左手放在肚子上；(C) 兩面附腳架的長方形立鏡，鏡面相對、面對面擺放；(D) 一名穿條紋睡衣的女生閉著眼睛、頭枕在枕頭上睡覺，畫面右上角有一個方位標示：上方 E、左方 N、右方 S、下方 W，女生的頭位於畫面上方，即頭朝向 E（東方）。

questions.stem:
What is the correct order to put the following sentences (a) to (d) back to blanks (1) to (4)?
(a) Hence, avoid this like the plague.
(b) This way, you “bought” the item, so it’s no longer a gift.
(c) Today, it’s bad etiquette and bad luck.
(d) It’s better to skip this “cheers.”
Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as something that would be affected by certain occurrence or behavior?
What is the most likely message the author wants to leave with Schöenberg’s story?

options.D: “There are two sides to every question.”

questions.stem: Which of the following pictures does this article advise against?

options.A: ［圖］一雙懶人帆布鞋放在木頭地板上。
options.B: ［圖］一名挺著大肚子（看似懷孕）的綁馬尾女生，一手拿著剪刀、一手放在肚子上。
options.D: ［圖］一名女生頭枕枕頭睡覺；右上角方位標示上方為 E（東），她的頭朝向東方。
